page.layout: One page of text in a single column; the printed page number and running head sit at the top right. Fragments of another page's text show at the left edge, outside the column; I have not transcribed them. Below the column, at the right, the catchword "Quæ-".

main_text.p: utilitatem & indignas nugas iam altè demersum eruatur: Hæc restat, & si modò capiant, sola penè restat ad Divinitatem via: Bellis istis & cladibus, quibus ferarum ritu in mutam necem sævimus hodie, non gloriam, sed proborum rependet æqua posteritas: & magna forte, quæ nunc veneramur nomina, audient olim ( quod sunt ) cruentæ belluæ & Humani Generis lanii. I, Amor sapientiæ: supple quæ subticeo: &, si visum fuerit, adde etiam acriora: Audes enim: A me quidem dicta, & frustra ferent, & non tuta.

page.notes: The text is printed in roman with italic and a few words in parentheses. Hyphenated line-end words are rendered with their printed hyphen (ca-piant, Di-vinitatem, ho-die, pro-borum, posteri-tas, au-dient, sapi-entiae, fo-rent). The word "proborum" is partly obscured at the line start and is uncertain. The opening fragment "utilitatem" begins a continued paragraph. The left-edge fragments are from the neighbouring page and were omitted.
